payload.task_text:
I am building a knowledge base for our university and need to create a structured course catalog from the learning management system data. Please look up all courses from the Fall 2014 semester, which are the ones with course codes ending in 2014J.

For each course, I need the course name, course code, the start date and end date, the total number of enrolled students (count only enrollments of type StudentEnrollment, including all enrollment states such as active and completed; exclude teachers and teaching assistants), the number of assignments, and the list of instructors (users enrolled with a TeacherEnrollment in the course) with their names and email addresses.

Create a page in our knowledge base wiki for each course. The page title should be "[Course Code] - [Course Name]". The page content should include the following information as text: the course code, the semester (Fall 2014), the start and end dates in YYYY-MM-DD format, the student enrollment count (StudentEnrollment type, all states such as active and completed), the number of assignments, and a list of all instructors with their names and emails. Create the pages in alphabetical order by course code.

Also create an Excel file called course_catalog.xlsx in the workspace with two sheets. The first sheet should be called "Courses" with columns Course_Code, Course_Name, Start_Date (YYYY-MM-DD format), End_Date (YYYY-MM-DD format), Student_Count, Assignment_Count, and Instructor_Names (a comma-separated list of instructor names sorted alphabetically). Sort rows by Course_Code alphabetically. The second sheet should be called "Summary" with a two-column layout where column A has labels and column B has values. The rows should be Total_Courses, Total_Students (sum of all student counts across courses), Total_Assignments (sum of all assignment counts), Largest_Course (the course code with the most students), Smallest_Course (the course code with the fewest students), and Most_Assignments (the course code with the most assignments).

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent performs the bounded seven-course source work directly, then uses one parallel writer wave. Canvas is read-only. Resolve the runtime workspace dynamically and freeze the exact Fall 2014 mapping returned by canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true): IDs 2,4,7,10,14,17,21 with their course codes and full Canvas names.

For all seven courses, issue ready calls in native-parallel batches: canvas_list_assignments once per course, canvas_get_course_grades(page=1,per_page=100,type=["StudentEnrollment"]) and the same for TeacherEnrollment, and canvas_list_course_users once per course. Student_Count comes from StudentEnrollment pagination.total_count. Teacher rows fit the returned page; if pagination says otherwise, follow it. When a roster result is oversized, read its complete full_output_path rather than the truncated preview. Join each TeacherEnrollment user_id only to its course roster, deduplicate by literal enrollment row.id, and sort instructor names alphabetically. Freeze seven code-sorted rows with exact full name, YYYY-MM-DD start/end, StudentEnrollment count, assignment count, and every instructor name/email, plus the six requested Summary metrics. Do not dispatch source or aggregation agents.

Wave 1 — start two Coder writers in parallel from that frozen table:

1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Sole writer of course_catalog.xlsx: create exactly Courses and Summary with the task's exact headers/row order and literal values, then read both complete ranges back.
2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Sole Notion owner for the seven titles `[Course Code] - [Course Name]`. For each title, exhaust `API-post-search`, filter exact matches, create at most once on zero with `API-post-page(parent={"workspace":true}, properties={"title":{"title":[{"type":"text","text":{"content":<exact title>}}]}}, children=[<canonical paragraph block>])`, reuse one retained page, and block on multiple matches or an ambiguous create. For a reused page, retrieve it and use `API-patch-block-children` only to add a missing canonical paragraph. The paragraph contains code, Fall 2014, dates, StudentEnrollment count, assignment count, and all instructor names/emails. Search the title again, require exactly the retained ID, and read its complete child-block text back.

Each writer self-corrects before returning. The main agent reconciles exact seven-code/full-name coverage, counts and instructor identities across the external workbook and Notion read-backs. No second wave or audit agent is allowed.

You are the SOLE writer of an Excel workbook for a university course catalog. Use only the mcp__excel__* tools (and mcp__filesystem__* if you need to inspect the directory). Do NOT touch Notion, Canvas, or anything else.

TARGET FILE (absolute path):
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-canvas-course-notion-wiki/workspace/course_catalog.xlsx

Create this workbook with EXACTLY two worksheets named "Courses" and "Summary" (if the create_workbook tool auto-creates a default sheet like "Sheet1" or "Sheet", rename or delete it so only those two remain).

--- Sheet 1: "Courses" ---
Header row (row 1) must be exactly:
Course_Code | Course_Name | Start_Date | End_Date | Student_Count | Assignment_Count | Instructor_Names

Then 7 data rows in EXACTLY this order (already sorted by Course_Code alphabetically). Use these literal values; do not recompute anything. Dates are literal text strings in YYYY-MM-DD format. Instructor_Names is a comma-separated list of instructor full names sorted alphabetically:

1. AAA-2014J | Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2014) | 2014-10-01 | 2015-06-27 | 365 | 6 | Dr. Abigail Martin, Dr. Andrew Walker
2. BBB-2014J | Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2014) | 2014-10-01 | 2015-06-20 | 2292 | 6 | Dr. Abigail Jackson, Dr. Clara Parker
3. CCC-2014J | Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014) | 2014-10-01 | 2015-06-27 | 2498 | 10 | Dr. David Rivera
4. DDD-2014J | Data-Driven Design (Fall 2014) | 2014-10-01 | 2015-06-20 | 1803 | 7 | Dr. Logan Wilson, Dr. Thomas Cook
5. EEE-2014J | Environmental Economics & Ethics (Fall 2014) | 2014-10-01 | 2015-06-27 | 1188 | 5 | Dr. Lucas Jones, Dr. Victoria Morris
6. FFF-2014J | Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014) | 2014-10-01 | 2015-06-27 | 2365 | 13 | Dr. George Allen, Dr. Isaac Lee, Dr. Mason Taylor, Dr. Matthew Davis
7. GGG-2014J | Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2014) | 2014-10-01 | 2015-06-27 | 749 | 10 | Dr. Andrew Walker, Dr. Laura Bailey, Dr. Ryan Adams

--- Sheet 2: "Summary" ---
Two-column layout: column A = label, column B = value. Rows in EXACTLY this order:
Total_Courses | 7
Total_Students | 11260
Total_Assignments | 57
Largest_Course | CCC-2014J
Smallest_Course | AAA-2014J
Most_Assignments | FFF-2014J

PROCEDURE:
1. Use mcp__excel__create_workbook with the filepath above (this may create a default sheet).
2. Create/rename worksheets so you have exactly "Courses" and "Summary". Delete any leftover default sheet (e.g., "Sheet1"/"Sheet") using mcp__excel__delete_worksheet.
3. Write the Courses data starting at A1 using mcp__excel__write_data_to_excel (data = list of rows, each row a list; include the header row as first row).
4. Write the Summary data starting at A1 on the "Summary" sheet.
5. VERIFY by reading back the FULL used range of BOTH sheets (e.g., mcp__excel__read_data_from_excel with start A1 through the last cell of each sheet, or use get_workbook_metadata with include_ranges=true then read the exact ranges). Confirm every header, value, row order, and sheet name matches exactly.
6. Self-correct if anything mismatches (fix cells, re-read) before returning.

RETURN (in your final report):
- The absolute file path.
- A confirmation that exactly two sheets exist named "Courses" and "Summary".
- The exact verified content of both sheets (you may paste the read-back rows).
- Any corrections you had to make.
Build course_catalog.xlsx

You are the SOLE owner of creating 7 knowledge-base wiki pages in Notion for a university course catalog (Fall 2014 semester). Use ONLY the mcp__notion__* tools. Do NOT touch Canvas, Excel, or the filesystem.

Create EXACTLY 7 pages (one per course), each with an exact title "[Course Code] - [Course Name]" and a canonical content paragraph. Work through the titles one at a time, in the order given below. All pages are created at the workspace root (parent={"workspace":true}).

TITLES (exact strings):
1. "AAA-2014J - Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2014)"
2. "BBB-2014J - Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2014)"
3. "CCC-2014J - Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)"
4. "DDD-2014J - Data-Driven Design (Fall 2014)"
5. "EEE-2014J - Environmental Economics & Ethics (Fall 2014)"
6. "FFF-2014J - Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014)"
7. "GGG-2014J - Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2014)"

PER-TITLE CANONICAL PARAGRAPH CONTENT (the page body; include ALL lines, in this order; note the leading "Course Code:" labels — use them verbatim):

Instructors: Dr. Andrew Walker (andrew.walker@openuniversity.ac.uk), Dr. Laura Bailey (laura.bailey@openuniversity.ac.uk), Dr. Ryan Adams (ryan.adams@openuniversity.ac.uk)

PROCEDURE for EACH title:
1. Search: call mcp__notion__API-post-search with query=<exact title> (page_size=100). Examine ALL results' titles.
2. Filter for EXACT title match (the page title equals the title string exactly, ignoring case differences is NOT acceptable — require exact equality).
3. Branch:
   - 0 exact matches: CREATE the page via mcp__notion__API-post-page with:
       parent = {"type":"workspace","workspace":true}
       properties = {"title":{"title":[{"type":"text","text":{"content":"<exact title>"}}]}}
       children = [ one paragraph block: {"object":"block","type":"paragraph","paragraph":{"rich_text":[{"type":"text","text":{"content":"<canonical content>"}}]}} ]
     Record the returned page id.
   - Exactly 1 exact match: REUSE that page (retain its id). Retrieve it (mcp__notion__API-retrieve-a-page) and read its children (mcp__notion__API-get-block-children on the page id). If the canonical paragraph text is already present, do nothing. If it is MISSING or different, append it with mcp__notion__API-patch-block-children using block_id=<page id> and children=[the same paragraph block with the exact canonical content]. Record the page id.
   - More than 1 exact match: DO NOT create or modify anything for that title. STOP and report the ambiguous title and the matching ids.
4. VERIFY after create/append: search the exact title again, confirm the only exact-match page is the retained id you created/reused, and read the page's child blocks back (mcp__notion__API-get-block-children) to confirm the full canonical paragraph text is present and matches the required content exactly.

SELF-CORRECT before returning: if any page's read-back content differs from the canonical content (missing lines, wrong numbers, wrong emails), fix it (append the correct paragraph if missing) and re-verify.

RETURN (final report):
- For each of the 7 titles: the page id (uuid) and a confirmation that (a) the page exists with the exact title, (b) the canonical paragraph content was verified present via child-block read-back, and (c) whether it was created new or reused.
- Flag any ambiguity or failure explicitly.
